class="article-prose"><section class="article-section"><h2 id="prepare-your-checkout"><a href="#prepare-your-checkout">Prepare your checkout<span class="heading-hash" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a></h2><p>Begin with the current ABI README and its toolchain and sibling-workspace prerequisites. The project uses nightly Rust and a checked-in Cargo wrapper. Do not treat a copied command as proof that every dependency is present on your machine.</p><p>Clone the public repository into your own development workspace, then finish the upstream setup instructions before building. This website does not execute these commands or provision a runtime.</p><div class="code-block"><div class="code-heading"><span>Shell commands</span><button type="button" class="copy-button" data-copy-code="true" aria-label="Copy Shell commands"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="15" height="15" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="8" y="8" width="12" height="13" rx="2"></rect><path d="M16 8V5a2 2 0 0 0-2-2H5a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v10a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h3"></path></svg><span>Copy</span></button></div><pre tabindex="0"><code>git clone https://github.com/donaldfilimon/abi.git\n' +
      'cd abi</code></pre><span class="copy-status sr-only" role="status" aria-live="polite"></span></div> <aside class="callout"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="19" height="19" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12 5c-3-2-7-2-10-1v15c3-1 7-1 10 1 3-2 7-2 10-1V4c-3-1-7-1-10 1Zm0 0v15"></path></svg><p>The repository may require additional sibling-workspace setup. Follow its current README before running the gate.</p></aside></section><section class="article-section"><h2 id="run-the-project-gate"><a href="#run-the-project-gate">Use the project’s validation gate<span class="heading-hash" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a></h2><p>The README identifies tools/check.sh as the primary validation gate and tools/cargo.sh as the wrapper for nightly Cargo. Use the wrapper rather than assuming bare cargo selects the intended toolchain.</p><p>A successful gate is evidence for that checkout and environment. Record the commit, toolchain and actual output when you share results. The commands below come from documentation; they were not executed as part of this website build.</p><div class="code-block"><div class="code-heading"><span>Shell commands</span><button type="button" class="copy-button" data-copy-code="true" aria-label="Copy Shell commands"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="15" height="15" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="8" y="8" width="12" height="13" rx="2"></rect><path d="M16 8V5a2 2 0 0 0-2-2H5a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v10a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h3"></path></svg><span>Copy</span></button></div><pre tabindex="0"><code>./tools/cargo.sh --version\n' +
      './tools/check.sh\n' +
      './tools/cargo.sh build -p abi-cli</code></pre><span class="copy-status sr-only" role="status" aria-live="polite"></span></div> </section><section class="article-section"><h2 id="inspect-local-behavior"><a href="#inspect-local-behavior">Inspect local behavior<span class="heading-hash" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a></h2><p>Once the CLI has built, the README provides local inspection entry points. Start with backend and scheduler information before enabling an external provider. Check what your process actually reports instead of inferring capabilities from a product label.</p><p>Live transports require their own configuration and explicit authorization. This guide does not ask for credentials, activate a cloud backend, or turn a local demonstration into a production service.</p><div class="code-block"><div class="code-heading"><span>Shell commands</span><button type="button" class="copy-button" data-copy-code="true" aria-label="Copy Shell commands"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="15" height="15" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="8" y="8" width="12" height="13" rx="2"></rect><path d="M16 8V5a2 2 0 0 0-2-2H5a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v10a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h3"></path></svg><span>Copy</span></button></div><pre tabindex="0"><code>./target/debug/abi backends\n' +

class="article-prose"><section class="article-section"><h2 id="prepare-your-checkout"><a href="#prepare-your-checkout">Prepare your checkout<span class="heading-hash" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a></h2><p>Begin with the current ABI README and its toolchain and sibling-workspace prerequisites. The project uses nightly Rust and a checked-in Cargo wrapper. Do not treat a copied command as proof that every dependency is present on your machine.</p><p>Clone the public repository into your own development workspace, then finish the upstream setup instructions before building. This website does not execute these commands or provision a runtime.</p><div class="code-block"><div class="code-heading"><span>Shell commands</span><button type="button" class="copy-button" data-copy-code="true" aria-label="Copy Shell commands"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="15" height="15" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="8" y="8" width="12" height="13" rx="2"></rect><path d="M16 8V5a2 2 0 0 0-2-2H5a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v10a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h3"></path></svg><span>Copy</span></button></div><pre tabindex="0"><code>git clone https://github.com/donaldfilimon/abi.git
    cd abi</code></pre><span class="copy-status sr-only" role="status" aria-live="polite"></span></div> <aside class="callout"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="19" height="19" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12 5c-3-2-7-2-10-1v15c3-1 7-1 10 1 3-2 7-2 10-1V4c-3-1-7-1-10 1Zm0 0v15"></path></svg><p>The repository may require additional sibling-workspace setup. Follow its current README before running the gate.</p></aside></section><section class="article-section"><h2 id="run-the-project-gate"><a href="#run-the-project-gate">Use the project’s validation gate<span class="heading-hash" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a></h2><p>The README identifies tools/check.sh as the primary validation gate and tools/cargo.sh as the wrapper for nightly Cargo. Use the wrapper rather than assuming bare cargo selects the intended toolchain.</p><p>A successful gate is evidence for that checkout and environment. Record the commit, toolchain and actual output when you share results. The commands below come from documentation; they were not executed as part of this website build.</p><div class="code-block"><div class="code-heading"><span>Shell commands</span><button type="button" class="copy-button" data-copy-code="true" aria-label="Copy Shell commands"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="15" height="15" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="8" y="8" width="12" height="13" rx="2"></rect><path d="M16 8V5a2 2 0 0 0-2-2H5a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v10a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h3"></path></svg><span>Copy</span></button></div><pre tabindex="0"><code>./tools/cargo.sh --version
    ./tools/check.sh

The README explicitly allows persistence to be disabled or unavailable, and requires those conditions to be reported rather than presented as successful writes. The former Zig tree has been removed. The CLI and MCP surfaces are documented entry points into that work. The scope of those interfaces is important. Source-reported contract coverage establishes a specific type of evidence, not an unrestricted guarantee of model quality, performance, or deployment readiness. Acceleration and fallback A preferred accelerator backend is not evidence that native kernels are linked. The README requires accelerated=false when the native path is absent and describes deterministic CPU SIMD fallback. Do not convert that fallback into a CUDA, Vulkan or ANE claim. A performance statement needs a reproducible artifact: checked-out revision, hardware, configuration, workload, method, measurements and limitations. None is published in this review site. Plans are not actions ABI’s documented browser command provides a reviewed local plan. The README says browser autonomy is not Current; actual navigation remains an external integration step. A plan displayed on screen is not evidence that a browser was controlled. Likewise, the small neural demonstration is not described as a production LLM. Preserve those boundaries in product copy, screenshots and examples. Similarity is a retrieval signal; it is not, by itself, proof that a result is correct or appropriate for a downstream task. ABI’s README associates WDBX with semantic storage and hybrid ranking. For exact interfaces and the Current/Partial/Proposed mapping, use the upstream source and specification rather than treating this overview as an SDK reference. Persistence is not implicit The README describes code paths that attempt configured storage and notes that persistence can be disabled, skipped, unavailable or unsuccessful. A system must distinguish those outcomes instead of fabricating a successful write. For example, the documented environment values ABI_WDBX_PERSIST=0 and ABI_WDBX_PATH=:memory: opt out of durable persistence for relevant paths. Check the source for the exact command behavior before applying an override to your application. What reported coverage means The README reports contract coverage for ordered search results, metadata round trips, segment/WAL recovery and compaction, temporal graph snapshot restoration, and MCP hybrid ranking. That is an upstream report; these tests were not rerun for this website. It does not establish arbitrary scale, deployment topology, compliance, encryption guarantees or throughput. The README requires accelerated=false when the native path is absent and describes deterministic CPU SIMD fallback. Do not convert that fallback into a CUDA, Vulkan or ANE claim. A performance statement needs a reproducible artifact: checked-out revision, hardware, configuration, workload, method, measurements and limitations. None is published in this review site. Plans are not actions ABI’s documented browser command provides a reviewed local plan. The README says browser autonomy is not Current; actual navigation remains an external integration step. A plan displayed on screen is not evidence that a browser was controlled. Likewise, the small neural demonstration is not described as a production LLM. Preserve those boundaries in product copy, screenshots and examples. A compelling explanation should not require removing a material limitation.","group":"Documentation"},{"url":"/docs/wdbx/","title":"Retrieval with its scope intact.","description":"Read storage behavior and repository-reported contracts as distinct evidence.","body":"Representations and retrieval In a vector-retrieval system, stored representations make it possible to rank candidate matches to a query. Similarity is a retrieval signal; it is not, by itself, proof that a result is correct or appropriate for a downstream task. ABI’s README associates WDBX with semantic storage and hybrid ranking. For exact interfaces and the Current/Partial/Proposed mapping, use the upstream source and specification rather than treating this overview as an SDK reference. Persistence is not implicit The README describes code paths that attempt configured storage and notes that persistence can be disabled, skipped, unavailable or unsuccessful. A system must distinguish those outcomes instead of fabricating a successful write. For example, the documented environment values ABI_WDBX_PERSIST=0 and ABI_WDBX_PATH=:memory: opt out of durable persistence for relevant paths. Check the source for the exact command behavior before applying an override to your application. What reported coverage means The README reports contract coverage for ordered search results, metadata round trips, segment/WAL recovery and compaction, temporal graph snapshot restoration, and MCP hybrid ranking. That is an upstream report; these tests were not rerun for this website. It does not establish arbitrary scale, deployment topology, compliance, encryption guarantees or throughput.
